paragraphs: In Trafford, which takes in Altrincham, Sale, Stretford, Urmston and Partington, children in care are looked after by Trafford Council's fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council recruits alongside the other Greater Manchester councils under the name Foster for Greater Manchester, and in October 2025 it hosted the Greater Manchester launch of a short fostering film, The Run, at a cinema in Altrincham. Its Director of Children's Social Care said then that there was an urgent need for more foster carers for Trafford's children.

The council sets out plainly who can apply. There is no upper age limit, you can work if your hours are flexible (though one carer needs to be available at all times for pre-school children), you can rent with your landlord's agreement, and not driving does not rule you out. A spare bedroom is essential, smoking or vaping rules out caring for under-fives, and everyone in the household over 18 has an enhanced DBS check. Training starts with the Skills to Foster course, and the council says it usually takes four to six months from first enquiry to approval at panel.

Trafford also runs Home from Home, a short breaks scheme in which children aged 0 to 18 with autism, learning disabilities or physical disabilities stay regularly with the same carer, giving their families a break. Carers already approved by an agency can transfer to the council, which offers payments and allowances, local placements, training and peer support.
Before you decide, speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies on this page about the children they most need homes for, the support they offer, and what they pay.

sources.title: New short film encourages Trafford residents to consider fostering (Trafford Council, 21 October 2025)
